claims.evidence: Round 1: addition chains at n=2,8,16,32,64,128 cost 1,639,588; 2,484,643; 3,777,256; 6,750,790; 14,306,701; 36,098,253 instructions. A terms-only DrPerf model leaves 54% own unexplained work in n=32..128, dominated by DeflatedExpression::clone and allocator/free/drop work. This supports cumulative prefix subtree size rather than only final tree size. cstnode.rs derives Clone for deflated trees. Offline least-squares fits on the six saved total instruction measurements: affine in n plus k*(k+1)/2 has mean absolute relative error 0.214%, maximum 0.608%, versus 30.2% mean error for affine in n alone. Round 3 independently changes the operator/assignment shape to annotated bitwise-or chains: n=8,16,32,64,128,256. DrPerf fits terms plus triangular prefix_work with 2.758% own residual, attributing the quadratic coefficient to DeflatedExpression::clone, allocator/free and drop work. Saved-total quadratic-model mean error 0.445%; the held-out n=256 prediction errs by 1.097%, versus 33.3% for the linear model.
claims.uncertainty: Clone and drop mechanism is supported by source-derived deep Clone and native attribution. Exact copy multiplicities are not derived from the external PEG macro implementation. Addition has offline total-cost validation, whereas union has directly marked quadratic-PCV blockwise validation.
claims.scope: Native parser; homogeneous left-associated addition and union chains. PCV models cumulative growing subtree size, not final CST size alone.

claims.uncertainty: Cumulative prefix size captures cloning growth, but allocator size classes, heap state, cache rehashing and identifier lengths leave residual. The exact prefix-size constant differs for alternating attribute and call nodes.
